description: We are a motivated and diverse team of students passionate about technology, innovation, and problem-solving. We combine creativity, technical skills, teamwork, and a strong desire to learn. Our goal is to turn ideas into practical solutions that can make a real impact. We believe that great projects are built through collaboration, persistence, and the courage to think differently.
summary: DISCOMICA is an interactive Planetary Intelligence and Scientific Discovery platform built to turn complex Earth observation data into transparent, reproducible environmental insights. While petabytes of open data exist across NASA Earthdata archives, fragmented formats, steep statistical barriers, and static map viewers make it difficult to uncover cross-regional patterns and multi-variable interactions. To solve this challenge, DISCOMICA unifies three core engines inside an interactive 3D Earth workspace: an Autonomous Earth Discovery engine that evaluates temperature, precipitation, soil moisture, vegetation, and water storage to build multidimensional Earth Change Fingerprints and identify Global Pattern Twins—distant regions undergoing parallel ecological shifts; a Scientific Evidence Engine that validates trends via Sen’s Slope, Mann-Kendall tests, change-point detection, confidence intervals, and Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery corrections while masking missing data rather than fabricating values; and an evidence-grounded AI Assistant with a Research Studio that explains statistical limits without inventing data and exports reproducible PDF, CSV, and JSON bundles. DISCOMICA matters because discovery without rigor is noise—empowering researchers, educators, and students to uncover hidden planetary connections faster and more reliably.
details: DISCOMICA (Planetary Intelligence & Discovery) is an interactive web-based platform designed to explore changes in Earth's systems through geographical visualization, time-series analysis, and statistical methods. The project allows users to interact with a three-dimensional model of Earth, rotate and zoom the globe, and select specific geographical locations using either direct interaction or manually entered latitude and longitude coordinates. Once a location is selected, the platform displays its geographical information and provides tools for examining long-term trends through interactive charts and statistical analysis. Users can also import their own time-series datasets in CSV format, specify the data source, variables, units, and missing-value indicators, and analyze the information directly within the platform. DISCOMICA applies several statistical techniques, including Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression, Sen's slope estimator, the Mann-Kendall test, and Median Absolute Deviation (MAD), to identify trends, evaluate statistical significance, and assess data quality. One of the project's main advantages is its combination of geographical visualization and scientific data analysis within a single accessible interface. It also emphasizes transparency and reproducibility by identifying missing values, flagging potential outliers without automatically removing them, displaying statistical limitations, and generating JSON records containing the analysis parameters, methods, and results. The intended impact of DISCOMICA is to make Earth system research more accessible and understandable, encourage interest in climate science and environmental monitoring, and help students, researchers, and other users explore long-term environmental patterns using scientific data. Its creative approach lies in connecting an interactive 3D representation of Earth with analytical tools, allowing users to begin their research by selecting a geographical location rather than simply working with isolated tables and charts. The platform is designed to serve as a foundation for a broader research environment that can eventually incorporate real satellite and environmental datasets. DISCOMICA was developed using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript, with Three.js and WebGL for three-dimensional visualization, Canvas API for graphical representations, and JSON for storing reproducibility records. The development process also considered scientific reliability, data quality, statistical transparency, accessibility, device compatibility, and future scalability. External scientific resources, including NASA Giovanni, NASA AppEEARS, NASA Hydrology Time Series, NOAA Climate Data Online, and KNMI Climate Explorer, are provided as references for obtaining scientific datasets. Although direct integration with these services has not yet been implemented, the platform already supports the analysis of user-provided time series and synthetic demonstration datasets for testing its analytical functionality. Overall, DISCOMICA aims to bridge the gap between complex Earth system data and accessible scientific exploration by combining interactive technology, geographical context, and transparent statistical analysis.
